- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is falling, model underestimates further decline; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 5–10% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model exhibits erratic behavior; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85 for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction to align with historical 30-day mean (≈78–80).
